clue.text: Simple craft featured in large collection

definitions.meaning: a basic floating platform of logs or planks lashed together
a great number or heap of things, as in a whole lot of problems

explanation.surface: A basic boat appears as one exhibit in a big museum collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a crude floating platform, and an informal word for a great quantity.

clue.text: Deprive of freedom others covering up short deception

indicators.note: covering up says the word for others wraps round the other piece

parts.note: the rest means the others, those remaining

indicators.note: short says the word for deception loses its final letter

parts.note: a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: Other people hide a minor fraud and so take away someone's liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict someone is to limit them, curtailing their freedom of movement or action.

clue.text: Upset by a furore the old have left for a few weeks

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the following words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Elderly people have walked out, upset by a fuss, after only a few weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BY A FURORE, with O ('the old') taken out as 'have left' says, are rearranged by 'Upset' into the month.
explanation.definitionFit: February is the shortest month, lasting only four weeks or a day more, so a few weeks.

clue.text: Try to get money from daily — it might result in fireworks

parts.note: to touch someone is slang for asking them for a loan or gift of money
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Asking a newspaper for cash might cause an explosive row.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUCH someone for a fiver is British slang for cadging money. Lighting the blue touchpaper is how a firework is set off.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchpaper is the fuse paper on a firework, so lighting it leads to fireworks.

clue.text: Better in the open, just the same

parts.note: out means in the open air or revealed
do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: An outdoor version is no improvement, just the same as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To better a rival is to surpass or exceed them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Dress G-man chose for disguise

indicators.note: for disguise says the letters are rearranged to hide their original form

parts.note: taken as written, its hyphen ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: An FBI agent picks a frock as a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: A G-man is an FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar and slit skirt.

clue.text: Training stupid people to undergo examination

indicators.note: to undergo places the fools as the ones going through the examination, so they follow it

parts.note: a physical is a medical examination
jerks is slang for foolish or contemptible people

explanation.surface: Dim people are sent for a medical check-up as part of their training.
explanation.walkthrough: Physical jerks is an old British phrase for keep-fit exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical jerks are drill exercises done for fitness, so a form of physical training.

clue.text: for instance, initially revealed in elementary book

parts.note: the clue's own number, 7, is an instance of a prime number

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word revealed

explanation.surface: Seven, say, is shown at the start of a basic textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue begins with its own number: '7, for instance' is a prime number, so the 7 in front is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is a simple introductory book for beginners, such as a first reading book.

clue.text: Right leg in part will continue to cause irritation

parts.note: the ankle is one part of the leg

explanation.surface: Something about one's right leg will keep annoying one.
explanation.definitionFit: When a slight rankles it goes on festering, causing lasting resentment.

clue.text: Case involving plot to work on newspaper

indicators.note: involving says the case wraps round the plot

parts.note: a suit is a legal case
a bed is a plot of garden ground

explanation.surface: A lawsuit about a conspiracy turns into a newspaper job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' wants to be a scheme; it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to correct and prepare copy for a newspaper, so to work on it editorially.

clue.text: Gladly send dog out to find insect

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone happily sends the dog off in search of a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A daddy-long-legs is a crane fly, a gangly long-legged insect.

clue.text: Blissful city with Welsh name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A city bearing a Welsh name is a joyful place.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small English cathedral city, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian comes from Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth, so heavenly or delightful.

clue.text: Drop a fraction, perhaps, on every side of hill

parts.note: round means surrounding, on all sides of
a down is a rolling chalk hill, as in the South Downs

explanation.surface: A small piece slips off all round a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Downs are the low grassy hills of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To round down a fraction is to drop it to the next whole number below.

clue.text: I am a trader without a flaw

parts.note: taken as written
I deal means I am a trader, dealing being buying and selling

explanation.surface: A merchant boasts of being faultless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I am a trader' as I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is perfect, with nothing lacking or wrong in it.

clue.text: Improper behaviour beats working, but manage to avoid dismissal

parts.note: a carry-on is a fuss or bout of misbehaviour

indicators.note: working says the letters of beats are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Misbehaving beats having a job, but one must try not to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an opener who carries his bat stays not out to the end of the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketing idiom for an opening batter remaining not out through a whole innings, so avoiding dismissal.

clue.text: Starting late, break in country's not obligatory

indicators.note: in says the shortened break goes inside the other piece

parts.note: nary is a rustic or dialect form meaning not one

indicators.note: starting late says the word for break begins a letter later, losing its first letter

parts.note: a recess is a break from work or school

explanation.surface: A break for the nation, starting late, is said not to be compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not obligatory' looks like the definition, but 'not' belongs with country's: nary is a rustic word for not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something necessary is required or compulsory, a direct synonym for obligatory.

clue.text: Diana, a German with long hair

parts.note: Hun is an old derogatory term for a German
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Diana, a long-haired German woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana was the Roman goddess of hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the huntress of Roman myth, goddess of the chase.

clue.text: Something used to catch salmon around Northern province

indicators.note: around says the salmon spear goes about the other letter

parts.note: a leister is a pronged spear used for catching salmon

explanation.surface: Fishing tackle for salmon is found in a northern region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern province' wants to be the definition; Northern is N and the province is in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four provinces of Ireland, in the east.

clue.text: Fee juror came upon suffering irresistible compulsion

indicators.note: suffering says the letters are in a damaged, disordered state

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A juror's fee came after much suffering under irresistible pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Force majeure is a legal term for an overwhelming power or event that cannot be resisted.

clue.text: Keeps an old form of punishment

definitions.meaning: holds as goods for sale, as a shop does
a wooden frame with holes that locked an offender's feet, for public humiliation

explanation.surface: Retains a historical punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a shop carries goods in store, and the old wooden frame for punishing offenders.

clue.text: Line of white-collar workers leaving South Africa

indicators.note: leaving says the country's letters depart from the word for workers

parts.note: the salariat is the class of salaried office workers

explanation.surface: A queue of office staff is departing from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a queue; it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a long rope or lasso, so a line in the sense of a cord.

clue.text: Time to worry about ringing sound

indicators.note: about says the word for worry is turned round

parts.note: to gnaw is to worry or nag at

explanation.surface: It is time to fret about the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a sharp vibrating sound, like a plucked string.

clue.text: The devil is about to damage one good-hearted man

indicators.note: is about says the devil surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Satan is the Devil
to mar is to damage or spoil
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Satan is on the point of harming a kind man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about to' reads as 'is going to', but 'about' is the container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A Good Samaritan, from the parable, is a person who helps strangers in need.

clue.text: Craftsman available from Christmas onwards

indicators.note: available from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tradesman can be booked from Christmas onwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a skilled worker in stone, a traditional craftsman.

clue.text: Creature such as a gryphon — treat him with care

indicators.note: treat says the letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Handle him gently: he is a mythical beast like a griffin.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fabulous hybrid monster of myth, as a gryphon is.

clue.text: Fishy smell a rat produces

definitions.meaning: to sense that something is wrong, to distrust

explanation.surface: A fishy odour is what a rodent gives off.
explanation.walkthrough: Adjective and verb: questionable, and to have suspicions; 'produces' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: as an adjective, of doubtful honesty; as a verb, to believe something is amiss.

clue.text: Saw it's fine to be admitted for meeting

indicators.note: to be admitted says the pieces are let inside the saying

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb
'tis is the old contraction of it is
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Someone sees it is fine to be let into a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb; it is a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting a need or requirement is satisfying it, as in meeting or fulfilling expectations.

clue.text: Employer starts to upset some employees' relations

indicators.note: starts to picks out the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A boss begins to sour staff relations.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs or makes use of something, so an employer in that sense.
